abstract:

Abstract: Learning semantically meaningful human movement representations from 3D pose sequences is essential for human behavior modeling. title: What DINO saw: ALiBi positional encoding reduces positional bias in Vision Transformers
authors: Moritz Pawlowsky, Antonis Vamvakeros, Alexander Weiss, Anja Bielefeld, Samuel J. Cooper, Ronan Docherty
abstract:
arXiv:2603.16840v3 Announce Type: replace 
Abstract: Vision transformers (ViTs) - especially feature foundation models like DINOv2 - learn rich representations useful for many downstream tasks. However, architectural choices (such as positional encoding) can lead to these models displaying positional biases and artefacts independent of semantic content. This makes zero-shot adaption difficult in fields like material science, where images are often cross-sections of homogeneous microstructure (i.e. having no preferred direction). In this work, we investigate the positional bias in ViTs via linear probing, finding it present across a range of objectives and positional encodings, and subsequently reduce it by finetuning models to use ALiBi relative positional encoding. We demonstrate that these models retain desirable general semantics and their unbiased features can be used successfully in trainable segmentation of complex microscopy images.

title: UltraBench 2: Towards Robust Evaluation of Vision Foundation Models on Ultrasound
authors: Ashwath Radhachandran, Adam Tupper, Christian Gagn\'e, William Speier
abstract:
arXiv:2609.28610v2 Announce Type: replace 
Abstract: Benchmarking is an increasingly critical part of research in machine learning and the domains where it is applied, including healthcare. Yet, despite the steady development of new ultrasound foundation models in recent years, the development of well-designed benchmarks to evaluate them has lagged behind. This deficiency has led to fragmented and inconsistent evaluations of competing models, making it difficult to measure progress. To address this issue, we introduce UltraBench 2, a comprehensive benchmark with wide anatomical and task coverage, and a focus on standardization, reproducibility, and ease-of-use. Using this benchmark, we compare existing vision foundation models for ultrasound image analysis. Our analyses demonstrate that ultrasound-specific pretraining still leads on classification, but that state-of-the-art general-purpose models have drawn level on segmentation.

Abstract: In additive manufacturing (AM), each change in part geometry requires a new thermal simulation, which makes design evaluation over many candidates costly. Geometry-aware models reduce this cost by predicting thermal fields on unseen parts with a single learned model, but they assume that diverse geometries are available centrally. Abstract: While federated anomaly detection enables the integration of local data insights across diverse nodes to reduce false positives, it inherently struggles with non-IID data. Abstract: This paper presents DeltaVisionX, a low-cost industrial automation system that integrates real-time computer vision with PLC-based actuation for object classification and sorting. authors: Ilyas Varshavskiy, Sergey Shulgin, Shuhrat Khalilbekov, Bonu Boboeva, Azizjon Azimi
abstract:

Abstract: Many applications of synthetic time series require a series that is much longer than the windows on which a generative model is trained. abstract:

title: WeatherDreamer: Learning a World Model from Multimodal Earth Observations
authors: Kate Duffy, Elise Penn, Tristan Ballard, August Posch, Thomas J. Vandal
abstract:

Abstract: Machine learning weather models now rival operational global forecasts but still start from analyses produced by separate, expensive data assimilation (DA) systems, which for global models are typically updated every six hours. authors: Omer Nezih Gerek
abstract:

Abstract: Classification heads built on conic functions give each class a bounded region of the feature space, and such regions are used to reject samples of unseen classes. title: On numerical issues of divergences between nearly equal distributions
authors: Brandon Amos
abstract:
arXiv:2611.18511v1 Announce Type: new 
Abstract: Barron et al. (2026) recently identified numerical issues in the softmax and soft cross-entropy loss. We show that similar issues are present in standard divergence operations between categorical distributions. This includes the forward and reverse Kullback-Leibler (KL) divergence and generalized Jensen-Shannon divergence (JSD), as well as Monte Carlo KL estimates and entropy. When the distributions are nearly equal, rounding and cancellation issues affect the forward and gradient computations. These issues can affect settings using divergences in optimization objectives, such as knowledge distillation, reinforcement learning, and proximal methods. We propose numerically stable reformulations and provide example implementations for each setting, validated by property-based tests.

abstract:

Abstract: LLM agents increasingly act over long horizons, where outcome-only rewards say little about which intermediate actions were good. title: Benchmarking AI risk behaviors
authors: Luhan Mikaelson, Robert Adragna, Emmett Brosowsky, Hayley Clatterbuck
abstract:
arXiv:2611.16318v2 Announce Type: replace-cross 
Abstract: We evaluate LLM risk propensities across a range of contexts and task demands. We evaluate models for how risk averse or risk tolerant they are in various conditions, as well as how stable and consistent their behavior is across conditions. We present a toolkit for developing model risk profiles that can be used to predict model behavior and which can be adapted to include new evaluations of risk propensities. We also examine how these properties have changed across model generations and families. We observe that 2026 state-of-the-art models tend to be more stable, more consistent, and more risk neutral than older models. These trends appear to be related; newer models are more stable and consistent because they are more likely to use expected value maximization as a decision procedure.

Abstract: Traumatic brain injury (TBI) often leads to subtle white matter damage that remains undetected on conventional MRI. Diffusion kurtosis imaging (DKI), an extension of diffusion tensor imaging (DTI), provides complementary information on non-Gaussian water diffusion and is sensitive to complex white-matter microstructure. With the advent of ultra-high-field MRI, the spatial resolution and signal-to-noise ratios (SNR) have been significantly enhanced, enabling more precise visualization of subtle abnormalities. title: PathOPEN: A pathologist-curated histopathology dataset for visual question answering

abstract:

Abstract: PathOPEN is a histopathology dataset for visual question answering. Abstract: Whole-body segmentation tools such as TotalSegmentator and MOOSE split more than 100 classes across five or six networks. The reason is memory. title: Pharos: Learning to Control Rare Events at Scale
authors: Jiajun He, Jacky Chen, Weiliang Luo, Heather Kulik, David R. Koes, Carles Domingo-Enrich, Yuanqi Du
abstract:

Abstract: Rare events drive transformations across physics, chemistry and biology, yet predicting their mechanisms and rates remains a fundamental challenge. Here we introduce Pharos, a framework that learns to make rare transitions accessible while predicting how frequently they occur under physical dynamics. authors: Anirudh Atmakuru, Tanya Goyal
abstract:

Abstract: Reasoning domains have shaped the post-training recipes of frontier models even though they are trained and deployed in domains beyond math and code. title: How Language Models Compress and Compare: Understanding Selection with Token Covariance Maps
authors: Moshe Eliasof
abstract:

Abstract: Many language-model tasks reduce to selecting among structured alternatives, yet we still lack a simple picture of how a decoder-only transformer organizes an entire selection prompt across depth. title: Run One, Get Two: Near-Free Streaming Safety Checks for Local LLMs
authors: Soheil Zibakhsh, Pedram Aghazadeh, Farinaz Koushanfar
abstract:
arXiv:2611.26975v1 Announce Type: cross 
Abstract: Local LLM assistants decode for one user at a time, so decoding is bound by memory bandwidth and leaves compute idle. Streaming safety checks today trade accuracy against cost. A dedicated guard model is accurate but nearly doubles the latency per token, while a hidden-state probe is cheap but less accurate. We present ToRA, an adapter that runs a second model as an extra row in the generator's decode step, sharing its weights and KV cache. Dual-row kernels read each weight once for both rows. On Qwen3-0.6B, ToRA matches or beats a dedicated streaming guard, with higher F1 on 12 of 17 benchmarks. It detects 11.8 points more unsafe responses than the probe at a similar cost, under 4% added latency per token.

authors: Mohamad Chehade, Hao Zhu

Abstract: Learning for optimal power flow (OPF) has recently been advocated to accelerate OPF solutions by using a pre-trained neural network (NN) to predict directly from given inputs such as the load demand. title: Weight-space programming and mechanistic interpretability for model editing in particle physics
authors: Rapha\"el Bonnet-Guerrini, Johann Ioannou-Nikolaides, Troels Petersen

title: Can pretrained Transformers deliver semiparametrically efficient inference?
authors: Han Yan, Jin Zhu, Chengchun Shi, Tengyao Wang
abstract:

Abstract: Semiparametric models provide a broad framework for statistical inference, yet efficient estimation typically relies on influence function correction tailored to each estimand and on nuisance estimation repeated for every sample. title: Decision Models for Multilingual Emotion Classification: A Comparative Study Against LLMs and Encoders
authors: Alessandro Piccolo, Francesco De Nicol\`o, Francesco Manco, Eufemia Lella
abstract:

Abstract: Decision models receive a question with a closed list of answers and return a probability for each answer instead of free text. title: EMA Policy Gradient: Taming Reinforcement Learning for LLMs with EMA Anchor and Top-k KL
authors: Lunjun Zhang, Jimmy Ba
abstract:

Abstract: Reinforcement Learning (RL) has enabled Large Language Models (LLMs) to acquire increasingly complex reasoning and agentic behaviors. title: GIST: Gauge-Invariant Spectral Transformers for Scalable Graph Neural Operators
authors: Mattia Rigotti, Nicholas Thumiger, Thomas Frick
abstract:

Abstract: Neural operators on irregular meshes face a fundamental tension. title: Inpainting physics: self-supervised learning for context-driven fluid simulation
authors: Jonas Weidner, Yeray Martin-Ruisanchez, Daniel Rueckert, Benedikt Wiestler, Julian Suk
abstract:

title: NucleoNet: A Nuclear-Aware Determinant Ansatz for Multi-Geometry Neural Variational Monte Carlo
authors: Qiao Gao, Yang Huang, Enze Hou, Yuzhi Liu, Jingrun Chen, Han Wang
abstract:

Abstract: Does post-training change what a language model represents, or how this representation is read out into an answer? title: Particle picking with an earth mover's seminorm
authors: Dvir Moshe, Amit Moscovich, Amit Singer, Ayelet Heimowitz
abstract:
arXiv:2611.27096v1 Announce Type: new 
Abstract: Particle picking is a key step in single-particle cryo-electron microscopy. It is a challenging task where tomographic projections of proteins and other macromolecules are identified in extremely noisy images. In this work, we introduce a particle picker based on a seminorm defined in terms of a fast wavelet approximation to the earth mover's distance. Our picker is template-free, self-supervised and does not require any prior knowledge of the molecules of interest other than their approximate size. We test it on three public datasets and show that it achieves state-of-the-art reconstructions.
